label: models/fw_drum.mdl: a rusted 55-gallon drum with a hazard stripe

measured.lineup: ours is one of A to D in lineup.png beside models/testsphere.mdl, models/gib_legbone.mdl, models/big_rock.mdl: the judge does not know which

M1.reason: The outline is a rectangular box in every view. The top and bottom views are squares, where a 55-gallon drum's would be round. The brief's drum is a cylinder, so the silhouette is wrong, not just off.

M2.reason: The measured size is 23 x 23 x 34, which matches the asked 23 across and 34 high exactly (sizeOff 0).

M3.reason: A drum's parts are missing: no rims or hoops, no lid or bung, no rounded body. The model is one solid block.

M4.reason: The surface is a flat, even grey with a mottled, concrete-like noise. It is near steel's grey, but there is no rust colour and no yellow hazard paint, so the regions are clearly off.

M5.reason: The hazard stripe, the rust, and any panel or rim detail are absent. The only surface is uniform grain, so none of the brief's markings or wear are there.

M6.reason: Side by side with Half-Life's own props in the line-up, it is recognisably a plain grey block (B), not a drum. A player would not take it for one of the game's props.

M7.reason: It stands upright on its base, as a drum does, and its height is along the vertical. Nothing marks a front, though, so the front cannot be checked against the brief.

M8.reason: The SMAK check reports no errors. It has 12 triangles, far below the threshold (twice the median of 62, or the third quartile of 156). The box is closed, not inside out, and not floating.
